Contiguous clusters of majority-group blocks

Source: R/seg_clusters.R
seg_clusters.Rd

Within each place, finds groups of adjacent blocks in which the group is a majority and reports the largest. Set against the population of an ideal council district, the largest cluster is a census-based proxy for whether a majority-group district could be drawn.

Usage

seg_clusters(
  blocks,
  by,
  group,
  total,
  threshold = 0.5,
  n_districts = NULL,
  bridge_empty = TRUE,
  contiguity = c("rook", "queen")
)

Arguments

blocks

An sf object with one row per block, such as the output of seg_blocks().

by

<tidy-select> Column or columns identifying the unit, such as place_geoid. Blocks with a missing value in any by column are dropped.

group, total

<data-masking> Block counts of the group and of the whole population. group must not exceed total.

threshold

A block qualifies when the group's share of its population is strictly above threshold. The default, 0.5, means a majority.

n_districts

<data-masking> The number of districts each unit would be divided into: a single number, or a column of blocks that is constant within each unit. NULL (the default) leaves out the district columns.

bridge_empty

Should blocks with no population join clusters? The default, TRUE, lets them; FALSE is a robustness setting. See Details.

contiguity

"rook" (the default) treats blocks as adjacent when they share an edge; "queen" also counts a shared corner.

Value

A tibble with one row per unit: the by columns, pop_total, n_clusters, and the largest cluster's population (largest_pop), group population (largest_group), and group share (largest_share, NA when there is no cluster). With n_districts, it also has n_districts, ideal_pop, largest_ratio (largest_pop / ideal_pop), n_viable, and n_districts_floor (see Details).

Details

Clusters are the connected components of the adjacency graph among qualifying blocks in a unit. Blocks in different units never join. Rook contiguity matches the usual legal standard for districts.

Blocks with no population, such as parks, freeway land, or industrial parcels, have no group share. With bridge_empty = TRUE (the default) they enter the graph, so two clusters separated only by empty blocks count as one. A district can include zero-population blocks at no cost in population equality, so a mapmaker could join the two clusters in one contiguous district. Empty blocks add nothing to a cluster's population, and clusters made only of empty blocks are dropped. With bridge_empty = FALSE empty blocks are left out and can split clusters; use it as a robustness check, since it can change whether a place has a cluster of district size. Either way, every populated block in a cluster is above threshold, so the cluster as a whole is too.

The ideal district population is the unit's population divided by n_districts. Two columns count clusters against it:

  • n_viable is the number of clusters with at least ideal_pop people. A cluster four times the ideal size counts once.

  • n_districts_floor is the sum over clusters of floor(cluster population / ideal_pop). Any union of majority-group blocks is itself majority-group, so this approximates how many majority-group districts could be drawn from majority-group blocks alone. It is a heuristic, not a bound in either direction: a cluster cannot always be split into contiguous pieces of exactly equal population, and real districts can add blocks where the group is a minority and still have a group majority.

Adjacency is found with sf::st_relate() in the coordinates of blocks. For longitude and latitude this treats coordinates as planar, which does not change whether two blocks share a boundary.

See also

seg_cluster_blocks() for each block's cluster, and seg_measures() for aspatial measures.

Examples

# A row of five blocks; the middle one is empty.
blocks <- sf::st_sf(
  place = "a",
  latino = c(60, 70, 0, 80, 10),
  total = c(100, 100, 0, 100, 100),
  geometry = sf::st_make_grid(cellsize = 1, offset = c(0, 0), n = c(5, 1))
)
seg_clusters(blocks, by = place, group = latino, total = total,
             n_districts = 2)
#> # A tibble: 1 × 11
#>   place pop_total n_clusters largest_pop largest_group largest_share n_districts
#>   <chr>     <dbl>      <int>       <dbl>         <dbl>         <dbl>       <dbl>
#> 1 a           400          1         300           210           0.7           2
#> # ℹ 4 more variables: ideal_pop <dbl>, largest_ratio <dbl>, n_viable <int>,
#> #   n_districts_floor <dbl>
seg_clusters(blocks, by = place, group = latino, total = total,
             n_districts = 2, bridge_empty = FALSE)
#> # A tibble: 1 × 11
#>   place pop_total n_clusters largest_pop largest_group largest_share n_districts
#>   <chr>     <dbl>      <int>       <dbl>         <dbl>         <dbl>       <dbl>
#> 1 a           400          2         200           130          0.65           2
#> # ℹ 4 more variables: ideal_pop <dbl>, largest_ratio <dbl>, n_viable <int>,
#> #   n_districts_floor <dbl>
